descriptive_title: Grade 2 Mathematics: Algebra (Coding) — Conditional Statements and Code Reading Without Screens (C3.1-C3.2)
short_description: A 5-day Ontario Grade-2 unit on coding without screens (C3.1-C3.2) framed around 'If-Then Detectives' — Inspector If the Conditional Cat and her partner Then the Action Dog. IF-THEN statements, writing two-branch code, reading code, altering code, and a capstone IF-THEN project.
long_description: Children spend a focused week as Junior Conditional Coders. Day 1 introduces IF-THEN statements with everyday and math examples (C3.1). Day 2 writes IF-THEN code with two branches for sorting tasks (C3.1). Day 3 reads existing IF-THEN code and predicts outcomes (C3.2). Day 4 alters IF-THEN code and describes effects (C3.2). Day 5 closes with child-invented IF-THEN projects integrating both expectations. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough covering misconceptions: always-true trap, missing-branch trap, input-doesn't-matter trap, alteration-doesn't-matter trap, missing-branch capstone trap.
what_is_included: 5 fully-scripted lesson plans with 50-minute durations and 250 minutes of total teaching time
5 student worksheets aligned to each lesson

10 printable teacher manipulatives plus 2 character puppets: IF-THEN statement cards (24), condition cards (12), action cards (12), input number cards (20), code alteration cards (8), capstone template, sorting mat, two-colour counters, TRUE/FALSE chart, detective poster, plus stick-puppet variants of Inspector If and Then the Action Dog
1 end-of-unit reflection sheet with 5 self-assessment prompts
1 two-row summative rubric covering C3.1-C3.2 across 4 levels
1 summative-administration guide tying the rubric to Lesson 5 capstone
Junior Conditional Coder certificate (one per child)
Detailed expanded walkthroughs covering common misconceptions
Differentiation tracks built into every lesson
target_buyer: Ontario Grade 2 teachers covering the C3.1-C3.2 cluster — coding without screens with conditional statements.
subject: Mathematics
pedagogical_approach: CRA progression. The sorting mat and condition/action cards are the anchors — children sort and combine concrete cards before moving to written code. Lesson 1 introduces IF-THEN concepts. Lesson 2 builds writing fluency. Lesson 3 reads code with traces. Lesson 4 alters code with re-traces. Lesson 5 closes with a child-invented capstone integrating both expectations.
